## What this deck is

::: {.content-box-marine}
[Two jobs, one file]{.box-title}

[Every class the EXTS revealjs theme provides, shown next to the markdown that
produces it.]{.box-body}
:::

- **For users** — scroll through, find the thing you want, copy the source.
- **For maintainers** — this deck is the theme's visual regression check. Edit
  `themes/exts-reveal.scss`, recompile, re-render this deck, and look at it.

::: {.footnote}
Source: `examples/exts-reveal-showcase.qmd`
:::

## Using the theme {.smaller}

Put this in your deck's YAML header. That is the whole setup:

``` yaml
format:
  revealjs:
    css: https://epfl-exts.github.io/exts-quarto-assets/themes/exts-reveal.css
```

. . .

::: {.small}
**The alternative.** `theme:` gives you more control — fonts, heading colours,
the title slide — but Quarto will not resolve it over `http`, so you must copy
`exts-reveal.scss` next to your deck first:

``` yaml
format:
  revealjs:
    theme: [default, exts-reveal.scss]
```
:::

Slide 4 of this deck **is** the example.

## Section dividers {.subsubsection}

...and this one is the other example.

## Section dividers — the source

Add the class to the heading. `.subsection` paints **oil**, `.subsubsection`
paints **marine**:

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
``` markdown
# A part of the talk
  {.subsection}

Optional standfirst.
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
``` markdown
## A step within it
   {.subsubsection}

Optional standfirst.
```
:::
::::

::: {.small}
Put the class on the same line as the heading — it is split across two lines
above only to fit the column. On these dark slides the theme also switches
**bold** to purple and links to a light green, because red-on-dark fails
contrast.
:::

## Headings and emphasis

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%"}
Every `##` starts a new slide. A `#` becomes a full-screen divider.

**Bold text is EXTS red.**

> Blockquotes get a grey rule down the left.
:::

::: {.column width="55%"}
``` markdown
## This heading starts a slide

**Bold text is EXTS red.**

> Blockquotes get a grey rule
> down the left.
```
:::
::::

## Content boxes {.smaller}

::::: {.columns}
:::: {.column width="45%"}
::: {.content-box-marine}
`.content-box-marine` — the key point.
:::

::: {.content-box-oil}
`.content-box-oil` — supporting detail.

::: {.content-box-white}
`.content-box-white` — nests inside.
:::
:::
::::

:::: {.column width="55%"}
``` markdown
::: {.content-box-marine}
The point you want remembered.
:::

::: {.content-box-oil}
Supporting detail.

::: {.content-box-white}
Nests inside a dark box.
:::
:::
```
::::
:::::

::: {.tiny}
Colon counts matter: `.columns` needs **more** colons than `.column`, which needs
more than the boxes inside. Get it wrong and the column renders empty.
:::

[Use `.box-title`]{.box-title}

[Not a `###` heading. See the next slide for why that matters.]{.box-body}
:::
::::

:::: {.column width="55%"}
``` markdown
::: {.content-box-oil}
[Use `.box-title`]{.box-title}

[Not a `###` heading.]{.box-body}

```
::::
:::::

## The `###`-inside-a-box trap

::: {.content-box-white}
Pandoc wraps **every heading in its own `<section>`**. revealjs treats each
`<section>` as a separate slide — so a box built from headings silently loses
everything after the first heading.
:::

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
[Breaks silently]{.box-title}

``` markdown
::: {.content-box-oil}
### My title
Body text that will vanish.
:::
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
[Works]{.box-title}

``` markdown
::: {.content-box-oil}
[My title]{.box-title}
[Body text that stays.]{.box-body}
:::
```
:::
::::

## Nesting, and what it does to colour

::::: {.columns}
:::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.content-box-marine}
Bold on a dark box is **purple**, and `inline code` goes light.

::: {.content-box-white}
Nested white box: bold is **red** again and `inline code` is back to normal.
:::
:::
::::

:::: {.column width="52%"}
::: {.small}
The theme flips **bold** from EXTS red to brand purple on any dark surface,
because red-on-dark fails contrast.

A white box nested inside a dark one is a light surface again, so it flips back.
You get this for free — there is no class to remember.
:::
::::
:::::

## Background images

Set the image on the slide heading itself:

``` markdown
## {background-image="img/figure.png" background-size="cover"}
```

::: {.small}
| Attribute | Does |
|---|---|
| `background-size="cover"` | Fills the slide, cropping the overflow |
| `background-size="contain"` | Fits the whole image, letterboxing it |
| `background-opacity="0.3"` | Dims it so text stays readable on top |
| `background-color="#425556"` | A flat colour instead of an image |
:::

## Brand colours {.smaller}

::: {.small}
| Variable | Hex | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `$exts-red` | `#cf0000` | **Bold** on light surfaces |
| `$exts-deepen-purple` | `#b741ba` | **Bold** on dark surfaces |
| `$exts-marine` | `#00a79f` | `.content-box-marine`, `.subsubsection` |
| `$exts-oil` | `#425556` | `.content-box-oil`, `.subsection` |
| `$exts-light-shade` | `#687a7c` | Blockquote rule, `.footnote` |
| `$exts-discover-turquoise` | `#35d48d` | 2023 identity green |
:::

::: {.tiny}
`$exts-marine` and `$exts-discover-turquoise` are **deliberately different**.
Marine is the teal the older workshop decks were built against; the turquoise is
the current identity green. The boxes still use marine so ported decks look
unchanged.
:::

## Cheat sheet {.smaller}

::: {.small}
| Class | Write it as | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `.content-box-marine` | fenced div | Teal box — the key point |
| `.content-box-oil` | fenced div | Dark grey box — detail |
| `.content-box-white` | fenced div | White box — nests inside the others |
| `.box-title` | `[Title]{.box-title}` | Box heading (never `###`) |
| `.box-body` | `[Text]{.box-body}` | Box body text |
| `.subsection` | `# T {.subsection}` | Full-bleed oil divider |
| `.subsubsection` | `## T {.subsubsection}` | Full-bleed marine divider |
| `.small` / `.tiny` | fenced div | 0.8× / 0.6× body text |
| `.footnote` | fenced div | 0.6× body text, grey |
:::

## Editing the theme {.subsection}

::: {.content-box-white}
[One thing to know]{.box-title}

[`themes/exts-reveal.css` is **committed, not built on demand** — it is what
decks load over `http`. After editing the `.scss`, run `sass` or your change
reaches nobody.]{.box-body}
:::

``` bash
sass themes/exts-reveal.scss themes/exts-reveal.css
quarto render examples/exts-reveal-showcase.qmd
```

::: {.small}
Full guide: `CONTRIBUTING.md`
:::
